5689.t: Probably an Anatolian loanword; compare Luwian [script needed] (tuwarsa, “vine”).

5605.t: From an earlier verbal adjective *δίπλατος (*dĭ́plătos), from Proto-Indo-European *dwi-*pl̥-to-s (“twofold”); compare English twofold. By surface analysis, δι- (dĭ-) + -πλάσιος (-plắsĭos).

5676.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₂w- (whence θεάομαι (theáomai), θῆβος (thêbos), θήγεια (thḗgeia)), an extension of *dʰeh₂-, with no clear cognates outside Hellenic; other extensions include θάμβος (thámbos) (< *dʰh₂n̥bʰos), τάφος…

5698.t: From καινός (kainós, “new”) + -της (-tēs, suffix forming nouns of state).

5693.t: From κατά (kătắ) + ἱζάνω (hĭzắnō, “to cause to sit”) with apocopic form καθ’.

5675.t: From the stem of τίθημι (títhēmi, “to place”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-, possibly combined with the stem of ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

5641.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wéikō, from Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to curve, bend; exchange”).

5654.t: From εὐ- (eu-) + a derivative of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ, “to stand”).

5687.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰrew-, the same root of θρέομαι (thréomai, “to shriek, proclaim”) and Old Armenian երդնում (erdnum, “to swear, take an oath”).

5603.t: From διοικέω (dĭoikéō, “to manage, administer”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

5666.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well, good”) + τάσσω (tássō, “draw up in order of battle, form, array, marshal”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix).

5664.t: From κόπτω (kóptō, “to beat, strike, cut”), possibly with the semantics being "easy to hit."

5647.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well-”) + λαβεῖν (labeîn, “to take hold of”) + -ης (-ēs, adjectival suffix).

5645.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁su-ḱlewēs (“famous”) (compare Avestan *𐬵𐬎𐬯𐬭𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬵 (*husrauuah), Vedic Sanskrit सु॒श्रव॑स् (suśrávas). By surface analysis, εὐ- (eu-) + -κλεής (-kleḗs).
